questions.question: You are starting a session in a new project folder and need to perform a series of complex, multi-step code edits. Which command is appropriate for starting this interactive environment?

answerOptions.rationale: Typing just the command name starts the interactive session where Claude can perform an agentic loop of reading, thinking, and acting until a task is complete.
This flag is used for 'print mode,' which is intended for one-off tasks or piping output to the terminal without maintaining an open session.
This command is used to pick an existing session from a list rather than starting a fresh interactive environment in a new project.
This command returns the user to the very last session in the folder rather than initiating a new interactive session.

questions.hint: Distinguish between starting a conversation and just asking a one-line question.

questions.question: According to the hierarchy of memory files, which locations are valid for storing a CLAUDE.md ledger to be loaded by the tool?

answerOptions.rationale: This is the primary location for project-wide rules, build commands, and coding styles shared by the team.
This file stores global preferences and personal habits that apply across all projects on the machine.

answerOptions.text: A specific package folder in a monorepo as ./packages/api/CLAUDE.md
answerOptions.rationale: Sub-directory ledgers allow for localized rules that apply only to specific parts of a larger codebase.
The hierarchy levels are limited to the specific project root, sub-directories, and the user's home directory (~/).

questions.hint: Consider the different 'shelves' of memory ranging from personal to team-wide to sub-directory specific.

questions.question: To prevent a custom skill from being automatically triggered by Claude's reasoning and ensure it only runs when explicitly called by a user command, you must set ___ to true in the SKILL.md frontmatter.
questions.rationale: The disable-model-invocation key removes the skill from the model's automatic selection list, requiring the user to manually trigger it via the slash command.
questions.hint: This setting refers to the model's ability to 'invoke' or call the skill on its own.

questions.question: A developer needs to perform a high-risk, large-scale architectural refactor that requires maximum reasoning depth and caution. Which model should be selected for this task?

answerOptions.rationale: Opus is described as the model for large refactors, gnarly debugging, and high-stakes tasks where maximum capability is needed.
Haiku is optimized for speed, quick questions, and mechanical edits rather than deep reasoning for complex refactors.
While Sonnet is the dependable default for daily features and bugs, Opus is specifically recommended for 'high-risk' and 'large' tasks.
Fable is used for the hardest, longest-running tasks, but the source specifically pairs high-risk refactors with Opus.

questions.hint: Match the 'bull-strong' model to the most difficult architectural work.

questions.question: What occurs when the 'context river' becomes full during a long session, and how is the CLAUDE.md file treated during this process?

answerOptions.text: Automatic compaction summarizes old conversation, but CLAUDE.md is re-read fresh from the disk.
answerOptions.rationale: Compaction summarizes context to save space, but the project ledger is a priority that is re-loaded from the source to ensure instructions remain intact.

answerOptions.text: The session automatically terminates, and CLAUDE.md must be manually re-imported using /memory.
answerOptions.rationale: The session does not terminate; instead, it uses compaction to manage token limits while keeping the ledger available.

answerOptions.text: Old messages are deleted permanently, including the initial loading of CLAUDE.md.
answerOptions.rationale: Messages are summarized rather than deleted, and CLAUDE.md is specifically protected by being re-read from disk.

answerOptions.text: Claude asks the user to manually delete files from the context window to make room.
answerOptions.rationale: The tool manages this automatically through compaction, although users can use /compact or /clear manually.

questions.hint: Consider the difference between summarizing a conversation and preserving core instructions.

questions.question: Explain the primary technical benefit of delegating a heavy codebase search to a 'subagent' rather than performing it in the main interactive session.

grading.modelAnswer: Delegating to a subagent allows heavy tasks like searching logs or large file structures to occur in a separate context window. This prevents the main session's context from being flooded with temporary search results, keeping the primary 'river' clear and avoiding premature compaction of the main conversation.
grading.rationale: Subagents operate in their own context windows to minimize token usage in the main session, returning only a summary to the user.
requiredAttributes: Mentions separate context windows or keeping the main context clear.
Explains that the subagent returns only a summary or report.
Identifies that this prevents flooding the main conversation with results.

misconceptions: Believing subagents have access to more powerful models than the main session.
bluffs: Stating that subagents are just for multitasking without mentioning context window benefits.

questions.hint: Think about the 'ferrywoman' metaphor and what happens when a boat is overloaded with cargo.

questions.question: When configuring a PreToolUse hook, what is the effect of having the script return an 'exit 2' status code?

answerOptions.text: It blocks the tool call and feeds the reason provided on stderr back to Claude.
answerOptions.rationale: An exit 2 code acts as a 'red seal' that cancels the execution of the tool and allows the agent to understand why it was blocked via stderr.

answerOptions.text: It allows the tool call but marks it as 'risky' in the session log.
answerOptions.rationale: Exit 2 is a hard block, not a warning or metadata tag.

answerOptions.text: It bypasses the permission prompt and executes the tool immediately.
answerOptions.rationale: Bypassing permissions is handled by specific modes or the 'allow' list, not by an exit 2 code.

answerOptions.text: It triggers an automatic retry of the tool with modified arguments.
answerOptions.rationale: Exit codes do not trigger retries; they signal completion (0) or a block (2).

questions.hint: Think of this as the 'red seal' that stops the clock's lever.

questions.question: You want to work on three different features simultaneously in the same repository without their file edits clashing. Which command-line flag allows you to isolate these sessions into distinct git environments?

answerOptions.rationale: Using --worktree creates a separate git worktree and branch for the session, ensuring file edits are isolated from other concurrent work.
While --bg runs a session in the background, it still uses a shared worktree unless a specific name is provided; the primary tool for repository isolation is the worktree flag.
Plan mode affects how Claude proposes changes, not how the repository files are isolated on the disk.
Model selection determines the AI's reasoning capabilities, not the local file management strategy.

questions.hint: This flag shares a name with a standard Git feature for managing multiple branches at once.

questions.question: To return to a specific point in a session and restore only the code changes while keeping the subsequent conversation history intact, you would use the ___ menu and select 'Restore code'.
questions.rationale: The /rewind command accesses checkpoints (up to 100 per session), allowing users to undo file edits or conversation steps selectively.
questions.hint: This command allows you to move backward through the session's 'checkpoints'.

questions.question: When defining a custom subagent in a .md file, which fields are required or commonly found in the YAML frontmatter to define its behavior?

answerOptions.text: name: The identifier used to call the agent.
answerOptions.rationale: The name field gives the 'contractor' a face and an identity within the session.

answerOptions.text: tools: A list of capabilities like Read, Grep, or Bash.
answerOptions.rationale: Defining specific tools limits the agent's scope and ensures it only has the 'hands' necessary for its specialized task.

answerOptions.text: description: An explanation of when Claude should delegate to this agent.
answerOptions.rationale: The description helps the main agent decide which 'contractor' is appropriate for a specific side-task.

answerOptions.text: max_tokens: The hard limit of the subagent's output length.
answerOptions.rationale: While models have token limits, 'max_tokens' is not listed as a standard frontmatter field for defining subagent identities in the source.

questions.hint: Recall the 'Contractor Rafiq' metaphor and what information he needs to be hired.

questions.question: Which permission mode should be used when you want Claude to propose a solution and allow you to edit the proposed steps before any files are actually touched?

answerOptions.rationale: Plan mode forces Claude to draft a proposal that the user can edit (via Enter) and approve before any actual tool execution or file modification occurs.
This mode allows file edits to happen without asking, which is the opposite of the cautious planning approach.
Default mode asks for permission before each edit but doesn't necessarily generate a holistic, editable plan for review first.
This mode removes all barriers, making it dangerous for large-scale planning as it executes everything silently.

questions.hint: This mode relates to the 'Planner's Drafting Table' where you review the blueprint first.

questions.question: Why does the source material recommend using '!`command`' syntax within a Skill's body?

grading.modelAnswer: Using the exclamation mark with backticks allows the skill to execute a shell command and inject its live output directly into the instructions at the moment the skill is invoked. This ensures that the instructions Claude receives are based on fresh, real-time data, such as current git logs or market prices.
grading.rationale: This syntax enables dynamic context injection, ensuring the AI works with the most current project state.
requiredAttributes: Explains that it injects live/fresh/real-time output into the skill.
Connects it to the moment the skill is opened or invoked.

misconceptions: Thinking it permanently changes the SKILL.md file on disk.
bluffs: Saying it is just a way to run tests within a skill.

questions.hint: Think about Maryam's recipe box and how she gets the 'current market prices' into her recipe.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a 'Skill' and the 'CLAUDE.md' ledger regarding token usage and session start?

answerOptions.text: CLAUDE.md is loaded in every session start, while a Skill is only loaded when explicitly needed.
answerOptions.rationale: Skills follow 'progressive disclosure,' meaning their full body is only added to context when triggered, saving tokens compared to the ledger which is always present.

answerOptions.text: Skills are stored in the cloud, whereas CLAUDE.md is stored locally in the project root.
answerOptions.rationale: Both are stored locally, though Skills can be distributed via plugins.

answerOptions.text: CLAUDE.md can only contain text, while Skills must contain executable shell scripts.
answerOptions.rationale: Both are Markdown-based; while Skills can use shell command injection, their primary content is instructional text.

answerOptions.text: A Skill can only be accessed by the user, while CLAUDE.md is only for the AI agent.
answerOptions.rationale: Both are instructions meant to guide the AI's behavior in the codebase.

questions.hint: Consider which one 'travels with the chef' every day and which one stays in the 'recipe box' until biryani day.

questions.question: When using the Agent SDK to build your own tools, the ___ decorator is used to engrave a function with its name, description, and input schema for Claude to recognize.
questions.rationale: The @tool decorator is the primary way to define the interface of a function so that the Claude Agent SDK can expose it as a capability to the model.
questions.hint: This Python/TypeScript decorator is described as 'engraving' the tool's handle.

questions.question: You need to ensure a specific CI check passes before finishing a task. Which command allows you to set a condition that Claude will monitor and work toward until satisfied?

answerOptions.rationale: /goal sets a standing objective that persists across steps, allowing the agent to continuously verify its progress against the specified outcome.
/loop repeats a specific prompt at an interval or until a condition is met, but /goal is the specialized command for tracking a session-wide target.
/compact manages context window size by summarizing history and does not track task completion.
/verify is a specific skill for running and validating an application, rather than a general goal-tracking mechanism.

questions.hint: This command acts as a 'direction-compass' that stays in memory even ten steps later.
